Summary: God's command to Hosea: take a wife of whoredoms and children of whoredoms as a sign of Israel's whoredom.
Commandment: Go, take unto thee a wife of whoredoms and children of whoredoms: for the land hath committed great whoredom, departing from the LORD.
Application: A prophetic sign-act command, deliberately shocking: Hosea's marriage pictured Israel's whoredom against the LORD (Hosea 1:2 states the reason). Rowed separately from the chapter 3 command because it is a different marriage act at a different time; parent may merge both Hosea rows into one sign-act row.
Purpose: To enact in Hosea's own marriage the LORD's charge against Israel's unfaithfulness (Hosea 1:2).
Function: A prophetic sign-act command, deliberately shocking: Hosea's marriage pictured Israel's whoredom against the LORD. This was a one-time command, given once to Hosea for a specific moment, so the civil, ceremonial, and moral division does not apply to it. Its goal was to enact in Hosea's own marriage the LORD's charge against Israel's unfaithfulness. The evil it addressed was Israel's spiritual adultery — looking to other gods. It restrained nothing by force; its work was witness, a marriage that preached the charge it embodied.
